drafted_from: tool:read-a-tool-setting row in tools/settings/tool-rows.json, do-work/read_setting.py, read-data/settings.py and test/test_settings.py; list:settings read with records:read
start_here: Say to your AI: "Read the settings I keep for the make-a-sample tool: try piece p1 first, then film f1, then my account, and tell me which row it used." It takes the rows from your list:settings and answers the settings of the most specific scope that has an active row.

lists.label: Settings
lists.holds: One row per tool and scope (a person, a film, a piece or the whole account): the settings that tool reads when it runs, as JSON.
alike: a settings sheet with one row per tool

instructions: 1. Pour the example setting rows into the list you keep tool settings in (see pour), or make list:settings from them; each row's id is record:setting:<workshop-folder>~<scope_kind>~<scope_id>.

2. Say "Read my settings for <tool>" and name the scopes to try, most specific first (piece, film, person, account); your AI reads the rows with records:read or records:list on list:settings, writes them to a file, and runs `python3 -I trillion-workshop/tools/settings/do-work/read_setting.py < request.json`.

3. Read the last line {"result": {found, id, settings}}: found true gives the id of the row used and its settings parsed; found false gives the default you passed. A retired row, a row written for another tool or a request with two rows and no scope is refused with what to fix (exit 2).

4. To write a setting, run it with {"make": {folder, scope_kind, scope_id, settings, name, tool, from}, "with_list": true}: the answer is the records:write input, and the settings are kept as sorted JSON text.

worked_examples.title: The film's pace wins over the account's
worked_examples.ask: Read my make-a-sample settings for film f1, falling back to my account.
worked_examples.given: From tools/settings/test/test_settings.py (class Reading): request.json is {"settings_record": <the rows read from list:settings: the account row make-a-sample~account~main with settings {"pace": 1}, the film row make-a-sample~film~f1 with {"pace": 2}, and a row of another tool other-tool~film~f2 with {"pace": 9}>, "folder": "make-a-sample", "scopes": [{"kind": "piece", "id": "p1"}, {"kind": "film", "id": "f1"}, {"kind": "account", "id": "main"}]}; the command is `python3 -I trillion-workshop/tools/settings/do-work/read_setting.py < request.json`.
worked_examples.hands_back: The last line is {"result": {"found": true, "id": "record:setting:make-a-sample~film~f1", "settings": {"pace": 2}}}: there is no row for piece p1, so the film's row is the most specific one. With scopes [{"kind": "film", "id": "f3"}, {"kind": "account", "id": "main"}] the answer is the account row's {"pace": 1}; with no row at all and "default": {"pace": 0} it is {"found": false, "id": null, "settings": {"pace": 0}}.

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for the same job and read it with records:read (its fields and row type). Run tool:pour-example-rows-into-my-list with that list as into and this kit list as kit_list: it matches each kit field to one of yours (your map, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), pours nothing under 80% and names the fields with no home, and otherwise answers the one records:write that adds the example rows beside your own.
